body: Thursday, July 16 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh appears firmly in a "prices are too high" posture, with markets pricing potential rate-hike risk rather than cuts. The 10Y yield has risen to 4.58% (+15 bps vs 4W ago), the 2Y at 4.13% (prior close, +6 bps), leaving a +42 bps curve that is positive but still flat by historical standards — a late-cycle reflationary signal. The Fed's Beige Book signaled an improving economy even as June CPI growth reportedly slowed, creating a "good data = no cuts" dynamic. Fiscal stance remains expansionary.

New / Most Important: The signal feed reports the largest US inflation decline in over six years — described as a "goose egg" moment on CNBC — yet this was immediately offset by renewed US-Iran tensions pushing mortgage rates higher and oil prices firmer. Retail sales came in below expectations, suggesting consumer fatigue beneath the headline disinflation. The Warsh Fed's July meeting will be his first rate decision as Chair, and the framing from multiple sources indicates markets now see the Fed as structurally more hawkish under his leadership than under the prior regime. This is a regime change worth emphasizing: Warsh is a "sound money" hawk who views asset-price inflation as a feature of his mandate, not a bug. The dollar surged post-decision, confirming the market digested this as a tightening signal even without an actual hike. Capital flows are responding — BTC is ripping (+7.4% vs 4W), functioning as a liquidity barometer that suggests the private sector is front-running eventual policy exhaustion even as the Fed leans hawkish.

Playbook ✓: S&P 500 at 7553 (↑0.6%) grinds higher on breadth rotation — Russell outperforming Nasdaq by 4.2% over 4W is textbook late-cycle broadening. VIX at 16.18 screams complacency.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The divergence is the Nasdaq 100 declining 2.8% vs 4W ago even as the S&P makes highs. Chip stocks are getting pummeled — SOXX selloff, SK Hynix diving, TSMC falling despite record profits. The market is telling you AI capex has peaked in its ability to surprise to the upside. Mega-cap tech is now a source of funds, not a destination. This is the kind of rotation that historically precedes a 5-10% Nasdaq correction while the equal-weight index holds up. The capital flow is unmistakable: out of momentum tech, into value, smalls, and real economy plays. Watch the Russell/Nasdaq ratio — if it keeps climbing, this is a multi-quarter regime shift, not a one-week blip.

Macro Stance: The ECB faces a brutal third quarter. Renewed Hormuz hostilities have forced a rates rethink, with the outlook described as "extremely volatile." Rising oil prices are pushing eurozone bond yields higher, complicating any further easing plans.

New / Most Important: The ECB selected 36 payment providers for the digital euro pilot — structurally important but not market-moving near-term. The real story is energy: Iran-related supply disruption risk has reintroduced stagflationary dynamics into the eurozone just as the bloc appeared to be stabilizing. This is the classic European trap — imported energy inflation forcing the central bank to stay tight while the real economy weakens. The MiCA regulatory framework reportedly left Europe "dollar-dependent" in stablecoin markets, another capital-flow negative for the euro.

Playbook ✓: ECB caught between growth weakness and imported inflation — textbook eurozone bind.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The digital euro pilot acceleration is faster than consensus expected — 36 firms is a large cohort and signals the ECB is genuinely preparing for CBDC deployment, not just studying it. If the digital euro goes live in any form by 2027, it will fundamentally change eurozone cross-border payment flows and bank intermediation economics.

Macro Stance: The PBOC signalled comfort with yuan levels and expects two-way moves (Bloomberg, [Jul 15]), and the yuan hit a four-week high (TradingView, [Jul 15]) even on a growth miss, which EBC notes barely moved USD/CNH ([Jul 15]). Easing remains in volume: liquidity to smooth tax payments and debt issuance (Bloomberg, [Jul 14]), with a floor that bills not be re-discounted below 0.5% (Reuters, [Jul 14]). Prices: June CPI rose 1% (Global Times, [Jul 9]) and producer inflation hit a four-year high (Reuters, [Jul 8]); Bloomberg labels the end of China's record streak of price declines "bad inflation" ([Jul 15]), cost-push rather than demand.

PMIs & Activity: Second-quarter GDP grew 4.3%, below the official target range (Bloomberg, [Jul 15]) and the slowest in more than three years (Euronews, [Jul 15]); first-half growth of 4.7% (Xinhua, [Jul 15]) remains "well within" the annual target on Beijing's framing (Global Times, [Jul 15]), but the quarter, not the half, is the signal. June itself was firmer: industrial output rose 5.3% y/y and retail sales returned to growth (BusinessLine, [Jul 15]), a surprise rebound (TradingView, [Jul 15]). The two retail measures differ: consumer-goods sales rose 1.3% in the first half (Ecns.cn, [Jul 15]), goods-and-services sales 2.7% (State Council Information Office, [Jul 15]). Investment is the hole, with the slide deepening as infrastructure joins property (Caixin, [Jul 15]), while exports jumped 27% y/y in June (Reuters, [Jul 13]) and the official manufacturing PMI was 50.3 (Reuters, [Jun 29]).

Credit Impulse: June new bank loans rose less than expected (The Star, [Jul 15]) and Bloomberg calls the credit expansion disappointing ([Jul 15]). That reverses May's picture, when total social financing grew 7.7% (CGTN, [Jun 12]) and topped forecasts (Bloomberg, [Jun 12]) on government bonds while loans missed (Reuters, [Jun 12]): now the headline and the loan book are both soft. Record consumer defaults undermine the push to boost spending (Reuters, [Jul 15]), and LGFVs that have added debt face curbs on new bond sales (Bloomberg, [Jul 15]). A central bank adviser is urging more debt (The Standard, [Jul 15]); the private sector is not taking it.

Property: Property investment slumped 18% y/y in January–June (The Standard, [Jul 15]), worse than the 16.2% fall in January–May (GMK Center, [Jun 18]). Prices are stabilising only at the top: first-tier home prices extended a four-month rebound (SCMP, [Jul 15]), while nationally new home prices declined at a slower pace (The Standard, [Jul 15]) and Reuters doubts a recovery ([Jul 14]). Developers face a fresh liquidity crunch (Nikkei Asia, [Jul 13]), and Vanke says its first-half loss may widen to $2.2 billion (Bloomberg, [Jul 10]).

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: Breakingviews says the GDP miss flags the cost of fiscal repairs (Reuters, [Jul 15]) and that the local-debt cleanup leaves a growth mess ([Jul 15]); Westpac sees a need for urgent stimulus ([Jul 15]), but Reuters expects support to stay calibrated ([Jul 14]) around a consumption plan targeting 60 trillion yuan of retail sales by 2030 (Caixin, [Jul 14]). Sinocism flags preparation for the July Politburo meeting ([Jul 13]). Trade pressure is building in Europe, where the surplus with the EU hit a record (Bloomberg, [Jul 14]) and a German engineering body urges broader EU duties (Reuters, [Jul 15]). Washington is softer: Trump's aides see China cheating on trade but shun reprisal (Bloomberg, [Jul 15]), and the Russia sanctions bill cuts the tariff threat from 500% to 100% (The Economic Times, [Jul 15]).

Markets & Flows: The Hang Seng rose for a fourth straight day to 24,681 on policy-driven buying of consumer stocks (BigGo Finance, [Jul 15]), mainland stocks held steady despite the GDP miss as investors shifted to consumer and financial shares (The Economic Times, [Jul 15]), and Alibaba and Baidu jumped on the Apple AI partnership (CNBC, [Jul 15]). SCMP argues the AI stock trade is intact despite a 10% pullback ([Jul 15]). Panda bond demand is surging (SCMP, [Jul 15]).

New / Most Important: June's data split cleanly. Output up 5.3% and a retail rebound show production and consumption holding, but loans missed, property investment fell 18% and infrastructure joined the decline, which is why the quarter printed 4.3% and below target. China is spending its income, not borrowing against the future, and the state is cleaning up local debt rather than levering it. Without a credit turn, the July Politburo meeting has to choose between a larger fiscal push and accepting growth at the bottom of the range.

Playbook ✓: Weak credit, a property-led investment drag, export strength and a stable, managed yuan are on script.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Markets bought the consumer rebound; the growth pulse says the binding constraint is credit and investment. That matters for the transmission abroad. Mining shares led FTSE falls as China's growth slowed (Yahoo Finance UK, [Jul 15]), the clearest read-through to iron ore and AUD from an investment slump of this depth. European exporters face a record surplus and a machinery lobby now calling for duties, so the policy risk is rising for EU industrials. Oil loses a marginal buyer as Chinese crude imports sit at a near-decade low (Bloomberg, [Jul 13]). EM Asia keeps the AI-export tailwind, and a stable yuan limits contagion to regional currencies. A rebound in loan demand, not another liquidity operation, is what would change the read.

Macro Stance: The BOJ is in an active tightening cycle but sending contradictory signals alongside the Takaichi government, rattling both bond and currency markets. The yen has weakened to what headlines describe as a 40-year low, with USD/JPY eyeing levels that trigger intervention risk above 160. Nearly half of Japanese firms report being hurt by BOJ rate hikes.

New / Most Important: This is a structurally novel situation that deserves attention. The BOJ is hiking rates into a weak yen — the opposite of what conventional macro textbooks predict should happen. Normally a central bank hiking rates strengthens its currency; here, the yen keeps weakening because the rate differential with the US remains enormous and Japan's energy import bill is surging on Hormuz tensions. The BOJ paused bond buying, leaving the yen even more exposed to intervention risk. Meanwhile, the Takaichi government's fiscal expansionism is running directly counter to BOJ tightening, creating an incoherent policy mix that resembles early-1990s UK pre-ERM crisis dynamics. Japanese SMEs are getting crushed between rising domestic borrowing costs AND a weak currency inflating import costs — a genuine credit event risk if this persists through Q3. EUR/JPY pushing into the upper 185 range confirms the yen is weakening against everything, not just the dollar.

Playbook ✓: BOJ tightening into a structural current account deterioration driven by energy imports — textbook terms-of-trade trap.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The fiscal-monetary contradiction between Takaichi and the BOJ is the divergence. If intervention comes and fails to hold, the next yen leg lower could be disorderly.

Macro Stance: The RBA is hawkish and media describes Australia as in the "grip of a lose-lose bind" — further rate hikes are on the table if US-Iran tensions persist, as energy cost pass-through reignites inflation. Westpac sees one more hike before eventual cuts.

New / Most Important: The AUD edged higher to near 0.6950 on hawkish RBA rhetoric, but the real risk is a fourth rate hike becoming consensus. Australia is uniquely exposed because it's a net energy importer with a housing market already under severe mortgage stress. A geopolitical-driven hike would be the worst of all worlds: tightening not because domestic demand is hot, but because oil-driven imported inflation forces the RBA's hand. This has echoes of the ECB's 2022 mistake.  |  Playbook ✓: Hawkish hold consistent with Westpac's "one more hike" call.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The conditionality on Iran conflict resolution introduces genuine geopolitical optionality into rate expectations — unusual for the RBA.

Macro Stance: The inflation picture is the best in years and the rate debate is moving the other way. Core inflation fell in June per the NBP's latest reading (Biznes Wprost, pb.pl, [Jul 16]), food is "cheapening the most in years" (Rzeczpospolita, [Jul 16]), and headline CPI was confirmed at 2.5% y/y with a 0.5% m/m decline (Miesięcznik Finansowy BANK, [Jul 15]). Yet the Council's hawks are louder: Business Insider carries a "surprising" RPP comment that hikes are more probable than cuts ([Jul 16]), following the member who contradicted Glapiński on Tuesday (pb.pl, [Jul 14]), while the governor's own offer of a post-holiday cut motion (StockWatch.pl, [Jul 9]) still stands after the Council kept rates unchanged (Do Rzeczy, [Jul 9]). The swing factor is fuel: the end of the CPN package will push fuel prices and inflation back up (Energetyka24.com, [Jul 16]), PKO BP expects a transitory move above 3.5% (PAP, [Jul 15]), Rzeczpospolita sees a food-price turn in autumn ([Jul 16]), and the energy and finance ministers are now weighing whether to bring CPN back (Polskie Radio 24, [Jul 16]). The FAZ verdict is "high growth, high debts" (Onet, [Jul 16]). Mortgage demand is solid with a new record average loan, though BIK expects declines and fixed rates are converging on variable ones (Rzeczpospolita, Bankier.pl, [Jul 16]).

Markets: Thursday belonged to Żabka: the stock jumped by double digits to a record after reports that Seven & i, the owner of 7-Eleven, is nearing a stake purchase (Reuters, Parkiet, Inwestycje.pl, [Jul 16]),. WIG20 still closed in the red despite it (XYZ, [Jul 16]) after Parkiet described consolidation around 3800 points ([Jul 15]). The card shows a rally that has rotated hard: Allegro 44.49 (+12.1% 1W, +17.2% 4W) and Orlen 145.5 (+4.0% / +12.5%), with Comparic noting Orlen +20% in two weeks and a new all-time high "within reach" ([Jul 16]), versus PKO 109.1 (+2.9% / +2.4%) and Pekao 235.5 (+0.2% / 0.0%) as the bank-tax threat (pb.pl, [Jul 14]) caps the sector. KGHM 313.4 bounced 5.3% on the week but remains -20.1% over four weeks; PGE 9.35 (-0.1% / -6.6%), Dino 28.55 (+2.7%), CD Projekt 231.9 (-1.1%), LPP 19850 (+6.3% / +4.4%). EPOL 41.05 is +3.2% on the week and +2.9% over four weeks, helped by a steadier currency. The zloty "no longer weakens" even as Trump escalates, with the euro suspended just above 4.32 (Bankier.pl, [Jul 16]) and FXMAG arguing the EUR/PLN rise may be ending ([Jul 16]); the card has USD/PLN 3.7657 (-0.1% 1W, +2.2% 4W) and EUR/PLN 4.3168 (+0.3% / +1.7%). The debt side is less comfortable: wnp.pl reports the latest POLGB auction "again did not go as it should" ([Jul 16]),.

Fiscal & Politics: The deficit crossed "another threshold" at 123.7 billion zloty after June, with the CPN programme exerting "powerful pressure" on public finances (TVN24, Gazeta Prawna, [Jul 16]); Business Insider says the budget is less ready for further shocks ([Jul 16]) and the opposition is calling it ruin (RadioMaryja.pl, Fronda.pl, [Jul 16]). Domański countered with KAS audit findings of 120 billion zloty of irregularities in public spending, about 3% of GDP, and 250 notices to prosecutors (TVN24, wnp.pl, Interia Biznes, [Jul 16]). The tax side moved: a decision was taken to lift the first PIT threshold to 171 thousand zloty from 120 thousand (PulsHR.pl, [Jul 16]), a revenue cost on top of the half-year hole. Construction began on a deepwater Baltic port meant to rival Hamburg (Brussels Signal, [Jul 16]). PiS wants Orlen to take over Qemetica; the state-assets ministry sees no basis (RadioMaryja.pl, [Jul 16]).

Corporate & Sectors: Energy policy clarified: the government's mix to 2040 is nuclear plus renewables instead of coal (Strefa Biznesu, Portal Samorządowy, [Jul 16]), an SMR roadmap is due by end-July (pb.pl, [Jul 16]), Stalowa Wola moved closer to an SMR with a Sejm committee approving land transfer (Portal Samorządowy, [Jul 16]), and PGE argues ETS changes could cut Polish power prices by 10 to 15% with the EU reform expected this week (Portal Samorządowy, Bankier.pl, Rzeczpospolita, [Jul 16]). KGHM wants to produce more of its own power to cut costs (Parkiet, [Jul 16]) and the Reda-Władysławowo rail line will be expanded to serve its future Pomeranian mine, an investment of up to 10 billion zloty (Bankier.pl, Strefa Biznesu, [Jul 16]). Retail: Dino is suing a union leader for 50 thousand zloty as unions prepare a strike, yet the shares rose on market successes (Bankier.pl, Fakt, INNPoland.pl, [Jul 16]); Allegro and InPost are back at the negotiating table and Allegro Pay now covers holiday bookings (DlaHandlu.pl, Cashless.pl, [Jul 16]).

Geopolitics & Security: Support for helping Ukraine has fallen from 77% to 52% (Rzeczpospolita, [Jul 16]), and attacks on Ukrainians in Poland are being described as "not the last incident" (Fakt, [Jul 16]). Poland and the Baltics continue to warn of a limited military or hybrid Russian provocation against NATO (European Interest, [Jul 16]; AP News, [Jul 15]), after Sikorski's false-flag drone warning (Kyiv Post, [Jul 15]).

New / Most Important: The Żabka bid is the single most important signal for GPW this week: a Japanese strategic buyer paying up for Polish convenience retail at a record price validates the consumer story at the exact moment the bank trade is losing its rate-cut and tax tailwinds. Set against the budget hole and a bond auction that disappointed again, the message is that foreign capital wants Polish equity cash flows but is pickier about Polish sovereign paper.

Playbook ✓: Zloty stabilising as cut bets fade is the expected sequence; strategic M&A premium in retail is orthodox late-cycle behaviour.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Headline CPI at target and core falling while RPP members talk hikes is a central bank reacting to fiscal risk, not price risk. A PIT threshold raise into a 123.7 billion zloty deficit widens that gap; if auctions keep underwhelming, the next move in Polish rates may be set by the bond market rather than the Council.

Macro Stance: Israel's economy contracted 3.8% in Q1 2026 — a severe growth shock reflecting ongoing conflict costs. Vietnam is being positioned for its "next growth phase" with efforts to rebalance capital channels toward a $1.5T investment target.

New / Most Important: Israel's contraction is among the sharpest in developed/near-developed market history outside of COVID. Vietnam's capital channel rebalancing is the more investable story — authorities are actively trying to shift from bank-heavy to capital-market-heavy funding, a structural positive for equity market depth.  |  Playbook ✓: Israel weakness on geopolitics is expected.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Vietnam's $1.5T investment demand ambition is enormous relative to current market cap — if even partially successful, this reprices VN30 structurally higher.

Narrative: The Nasdaq 100 is down 2.8% vs 4W ago while the S&P makes new highs: money is rotating out of mega-cap tech, chipmakers are dragging the sector and AI-spending scrutiny is intensifying ahead of Big Tech earnings.

Reported: IBM plunged 25% after a second-quarter warning, its CEO admitting the company fell behind (Fortune, [Jul 15]), and Oppenheimer cut the stock (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 15]). Ericsson missed Q2 estimates (Investing.com, [Jul 14]). Tata Elxsi fell nearly 7% as profit, EBIT and margins missed (India Infoline, [Jul 15]).

EPS Upside Watch: Apple — quietly at a record high and up 20% in 2026 (24/7 Wall St., [Jul 15]), re-rated as defensive tech. Arista Networks — the stock is rising on AI networking, and TIKR asks whether Wall Street gives it enough credit (TIKR.com, [Jul 15]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The Nasdaq trailing the Russell 2000 by 4.2% over four weeks reverses the concentration trade that has defined markets since 2023. When the biggest names become a source of funds, the reversal tends to be violent and multi-month.

Narrative: Meta faces AI-spending scrutiny, with Wedbush preferring Google and Amazon for hyperscaler exposure; Meta's data-centre plans are pitched as a fix for its capex problem, but markets remain sceptical.
Reported: No major reports this week; Netflix reports on July 16 (tastylive, [Jul 15]).
EPS Upside Watch: Alphabet — earnings are expected to grow ahead of next week's release (Yahoo Finance Australia, [Jul 15]), with Google Cloud growth, TPU sales and Gemini in focus (IG, [Jul 15]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Netflix hasn't been this cheap in 21 months, yet analysts are growing more cautious (Benzinga, [Jul 15]). The sell side is chasing AI-capex platforms and shunning the cheapest pure content play, so a clean print would meet low expectations.
Narrative: Rising yields (10Y at 4.58%, +15 bps) and a positively sloped but still-flat +42 bps curve are a modest NIM tailwind, and record trading and dealmaking are doing the rest.

Reported: Morgan Stanley posted record quarterly revenue and profit as equities trading surged 69% (CNBC, [Jul 15]). JPMorgan posted the highest quarterly profit ever by a US bank (Reuters, [Jul 14]). BlackRock beat as assets hit $15.34T (Quartz, [Jul 15]), and BNY lifted its 2026 revenue forecast above estimates (Reuters, [Jul 15]).
EPS Upside Watch: Bank of America — Morningstar says don't be surprised if net interest income overdelivers (Morningstar, [Jul 15]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Visa launching a stablecoin platform for minting, wallets and payments says TradFi sees stablecoins as complementary, not competitive. Whoever controls the on/off ramps controls the toll booth; watch Mastercard's response.

Narrative: WTI at 78.47 (↑3.2% vs 4W) holds near a one-month high on US-Iran tensions. The bid is supply, not Chinese demand: China's second-quarter growth slowed to 4.3% and its crude imports fell to the lowest in nearly a decade.
Reported: BP expects stronger Q2 earnings despite lower output (Kalkine Media, [Jul 14]) and sees a boost from energy prices, but flags a $1 billion impairment (Reuters, [Jul 14]).

EPS Upside Watch: Devon Energy — earnings expectations upgraded on estimate revisions (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 10]). Cameco — a Q2 preview argues earnings could restart the nuclear rally (Seeking Alpha, [Jul 13]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Oil prices "reflect complacency about ceasefire" while central banks reprice for energy-driven inflation. That is incoherent: either oil stays high and policy tightens further, or oil falls and rate relief arrives — one leg has to break.
Narrative: Transportation stocks are helping fuel the rally, and the Russell 2000's outperformance (↑1.3% vs 4W, 4.2% ahead of the Nasdaq) favours industrials given their small-cap weight.

Reported: United beat Q2 estimates and raised its full-year forecast (Quartz, [Jul 15]) despite expecting $6 billion in added fuel costs (CNBC, [Jul 15]). J.B. Hunt rose 9% on a Q2 beat (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 15]). Pentair plunged after a guidance cut and a surprise CFO exit (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 15]).
EPS Upside Watch: GE Aerospace — RBC says it could raise 2026 guidance by $500 million (Benzinga, [Jul 15]). Caterpillar — JPMorgan and Wells Fargo just raised their targets (TIKR.com, [Jul 15]).
⚡ Breaking Convention: Airlines are supposed to be fuel victims, yet United lifted its outlook as higher fares blunt fuel prices (WSJ, [Jul 15]). Pricing power, not jet fuel, is setting the margins.
Narrative: US retail sales rose less than expected, pointing to consumer fatigue, and the cost-cutting cycle is deepening in consumer-facing names.

Reported: Richemont's sales beat lifted the luxury sector as jewellery shines (Reuters, [Jul 15]). Fast Retailing raised its profit forecast while cautioning on the yen and heatwaves (Reuters, [Jul 9]). Rank Group raised profit guidance on digital growth and gaming machines (Yahoo Finance UK, [Jul 14]).

EPS Upside Watch: Amazon — Jefferies' top Mag 7 pick into Q2, ahead of Tesla and Apple (24/7 Wall St., [Jul 15]). Marriott — raised guidance again while analysts still target just $381 (TIKR.com, [Jul 10]), leaving estimates behind the company.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Luxury is rallying while mass retail fades, but the sector still needs China (MarketWatch, [Jul 15]). The beat came from the asset-rich consumer, so the fatigue in retail sales is a mass-market problem, not a luxury one.

Narrative: Cooling pricing pressures are directly bullish for staples margins as input costs ease while brands keep pricing power, and the sector is a classic beneficiary of defensive rotation in a rising-rate, tech-out tape.

Reported: Conagra fell as guidance disappointed and it cut its dividend (Barron's, [Jul 15]), alongside a $2 billion charge (MarketWatch, [Jul 15]). PepsiCo's turnaround stutters as Americans rethink snacking (ET BrandEquity, [Jul 15]). Simply Good Foods rose as earnings and revenue topped estimates (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 9]).
EPS Upside Watch: Seven & i — the 7-Eleven owner raised guidance as gas earnings rose at its North America unit (WSJ, [Jul 9]), a fuel-margin tailwind.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The bullish margin story is not reaching packaged food: after Conagra's cut, Barron's lists 6 more food stock payouts at risk (Barron's, [Jul 15]). Volumes, not input costs, are the binding constraint.

Narrative: Healthcare benefits from the same rotation that favours defensives over growth, and rising yields hurt it less than long-duration tech; medtech demand is holding up in a slowing consumer economy.

Reported: J&J beat Q2 estimates and raised full-year guidance (Yahoo Finance UK, [Jul 15]), but a medtech miss overshadowed the beat (Reuters, [Jul 15]). Elevance raised guidance on lower-than-expected medical costs (Bloomberg.com, [Jul 15]), yet the stock fell on Medicaid spending worries (Barron's, [Jul 15]).

EPS Upside Watch: UnitedHealth — analysts see improving medical cost trends into its report (Seeking Alpha, [Jul 15]). Eli Lilly — Bernstein raised its target on beat potential (Investing.com, [Jul 14]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Coverage, not cost, is the new risk: HCA cut its forecast on insurance coverage losses (Healthcare Dive, [Jul 14]) and Elevance fell on Medicaid despite a raise, so payer mix can hurt a sector assumed to be volume-safe.

Narrative: Copper at 6.34 (↓2.3% vs 4W) trades as an AI data-centre and grid-capex metal and is dipping with the chip sell-off, while gold miners sink. The cyclical read comes from China's investment data: property investment slumped 18% y/y in January–June and infrastructure has joined the decline.

Reported: BASF lifted its guidance as higher chemical prices boost earnings (Bloomberg.com, [Jul 15]) but warned on Iran-war risks (Reuters, [Jul 15]). Himadri Speciality posted record Q1 revenue with profit up 26% (CNBC TV18, [Jul 15]).
EPS Upside Watch: Rio Tinto — cut its copper cost guidance as the Pilbara posted its biggest half since 2018 (Market Index, [Jul 15]); lower unit costs on an AI and grid-capex metal widen margins.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Gold at 3997, down 7.7% while Iran and Hormuz risk escalates, is a major narrative break: the trade was overcrowded, and BTC outperforming gold by 15.1 points over four weeks suggests it is taking gold's macro-hedge bid.
Narrative: Mortgage rates rose again on Iran tensions, and with the 10Y at 4.58% and climbing under a hawkish Warsh Fed, the rate-sensitive REIT complex stays under pressure.

Reported: China Vanke says its first-half loss may widen to $2.2 billion (Bloomberg.com, [Jul 10]). UK homebuilder MJ Gleeson cited an uncertain outlook amid geopolitical and policy risks (Global Banking & Finance Review, [Jul 10]).

EPS Upside Watch: Prologis — its Q2 preview asks whether healthy leasing can support earnings (TradingView, [Jul 15]). Schroder REIT — portfolio vacancies are at a four-year low (Investment Week, [Jul 10]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The equity window is open despite rates: Supermarket Income REIT launched a £100 million fundraise to expand (Yahoo Finance UK, [Jul 15]) and Picton bidders raised their offer (Property Week, [Jul 10]). Capital is still pricing REIT assets above the bearish consensus.

Narrative: Rising yields are a headwind for the sector's bond-proxy status, but AI data-centre power demand is an offsetting secular tailwind, and Meta's data-centre expansion plans keep that story alive.
Reported: No major reports this week.
EPS Upside Watch: Vistra — long-term PPAs are seen as a growth catalyst (TradingView, [Jul 9]), locking in contracted power sales.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Data-centre demand has investors re-evaluating US electric utility stocks (S&P Global, [Jul 10]). If the group is re-rated as a growth sector rather than a bond proxy, the rate headwind matters less than the consensus assumes.

Narrative: Rising oil prices and ECB rate uncertainty are a double headwind, with European consumer weakness and the tariff overhang on top; Germany's auto industry is scaling back its ambitions (Automotive News, [Jul 15]).

Reported: No major reports this week. Q2 deliveries set the tone: German carmakers' China sales plunged 30%-41% (Fortune, [Jul 11]), and BMW's car sales declined after a 30% plunge in China (Bloomberg.com, [Jul 10]).
EPS Upside Watch: None flagged.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The China price war is now hurting the attackers: Changan warns first-half net profit could plunge nearly 70% (finance.biggo.com, [Jul 14]) and GWM flags a sharp drop (CnEVPost, [Jul 14]). If Chinese makers retreat on price, pressure on European margins could ease.
Narrative: The chip complex is in outright liquidation: SK Hynix dove after its $30B debut and the SOX got "socked again", pressuring equity indices globally even as the fundamentals keep improving.
